findings.title: canView(client) ignores per-client policies when the caller has type-level VIEW
findings.body: canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() is true, and canView() is true for any caller holding VIEW on the all-'Clients' resource. In that case the per-client resource is never evaluated, so a negative or otherwise non-matching per-client VIEW permission is silently ignored and the client stays visible and listable. canManage(client) and hasPermission(client, ...) treat an existing per-client resource as overriding the type-level grant, and the users tests (testViewUserPermission) establish that per-object deny overrides the all-users VIEW grant. This method is inconsistent with that and lets an explicit deny be bypassed. No test covers a per-client deny on top of an all-clients VIEW grant.

findings.title: setPermissionsEnabled throws, so the ClientRemovedEvent listener fails client deletion under V2
findings.body: Before this PR MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited clients() from MgmtPermissions, so setPermissionsEnabled worked. Now clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled) throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent, and management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when the V2 flag is on. When the listener is active (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled alongside V2), deleting any client throws during event dispatch and the deletion request fails.

findings.title: Removal listener gated on the V1 flag; V2-only deployments lose cleanup silently
findings.body: The whole listener (role, client and group removal cleanup) is now wrapped in Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, the V1 flag, while the calls it makes dispatch to MgmtPermissionsV2 when the V2 flag is on. With only V2 enabled, deleting a client, group or role no longer runs any cleanup. Nothing replaces it: ClientPermissionsV2 has no removal path, so the per-client admin-permissions resource (named by the client UUID) and its attached policies stay behind. The gate is not mentioned in the PR description. The gate should follow the flag that governs the active evaluator, and V2 cleanup should be implemented rather than suppressed.

findings.title: V2 branch of the 4-arg evaluator() drops the target realm
findings.body: In the V2 branch, evaluator(session, realm, adminsRealm, admin) calls new MgmtPermissionsV2(session, adminsRealm, admin) and never passes realm, although MgmtPermissionsV2 has a 4-argument constructor (session, realm, adminsRealm, admin) that carries it. The V1 branch passes realm. This PR makes MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() build ClientPermissionsV2 from the realm field. Client permission checks made through this factory may therefore be evaluated against the admin's realm rather than the target realm, depending on what the 3-argument constructor assigns to realm.

findings.title: init() never backfills the Clients resource type or new scopes for existing realms
findings.body: init() returns early when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms set up with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 before this change never receive the new 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope' and 'map-roles-composite' scopes or the 'Clients' all-resource, and nothing else backfills them. For such realms, creating a CLIENTS permission hits 'No scopes found.' (line 108), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(client, ...) passes a null resource into findByResource (ClientPermissionsV2 line 219) whenever no per-client resource exists. That will fail with an NPE or wrong result on client checks. No migration or test covers this path.

findings.title: Type-level grant is ignored when a per-client resource exists, contradicting the documented 'also if' contract
findings.body: hasPermission(client, scope) consults the all-'Clients' resource only when no per-client resource exists. If a per-client resource exists (for example because some other client-specific permission was created), only that resource's policies are evaluated. A caller with MANAGE on all clients is then denied canManage(X) for such a client. The interface Javadoc added in this PR (ClientPermissionEvaluator) says canManage, canView, canConfigure and canMap* are also true for the 'all clients' permission, which this does not honor. Either the documentation or the precedence rule must change. canView(client) applies the opposite precedence, so the two methods disagree.

findings.title: Inherited permission methods now throw UnsupportedOperationException on reachable paths
findings.body: canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, the mapRoles/manage/configure/view permission factories, resource(), getPermissions(), isPermissionsEnabled() and setPermissionsEnabled() all throw UnsupportedOperationException. Previously clients() under V2 returned the inherited V1 implementation. These are methods of the public evaluator interface that existing code calls (for example the legacy token-exchange check calls canExchangeTo, and client management-permission endpoints call getPermissions/resource). A request that reaches them now fails with HTTP 500 instead of a denial or a valid response. Nothing in the PR shows that callers are guarded.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the literal 'Clients' and omits type-level grants
findings.body: findByType(server, 'Clients', ...) also returns the all-clients resource itself, since its name and type are both 'Clients' (created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init). If the caller holds the scope on it, the string 'Clients' is added to the result as if it were a client id. Clients covered only by a type-level grant are never added, because only per-client resources are inspected, whereas hasPermission(client, ...) falls back to the type-level resource. The result therefore disagrees with canView/canManage for the same caller.

findings.title: getResourceName has no CLIENTS branch, so client permission resources get no readable name
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases USERS to return the username. There is no CLIENTS branch, so client resources fall back to resource.getDisplayName(). getOrCreateResource never sets a display name for client resources, so the name shown for a client permission would be null or the internal UUID rather than the clientId. The PR adds no mapping and no test for it.

findings.title: void require* methods documented as 'Returns true'
findings.body: requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() are void methods, but their Javadoc says 'Returns {@code true} if ...'. They should say they throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding can* method returns false, as the other require* methods in this interface do.

findings.title: canView(client) repeats full policy evaluations for every client in a listing
findings.body: canView(client) first calls canView(), which evaluates the all-clients resource, then canConfigure(client), which evaluates canManage(client) and hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE), and finally hasPermission(client, VIEW). Each hasPermission call does a resource lookup and a full evaluatePermission. Checking each client in a list therefore costs several policy evaluations per client, and the type-level evaluation is repeated N times. Nothing caches the type-level result.
